admissions_overview.summary: Admission to Ugandan universities is through each institution, and a first degree normally requires the Uganda Certificate of Education (UCE, O-Level) and the Uganda Advanced Certificate of Education (UACE, A-Level) with the principal and subsidiary passes that each programme asks for. Public universities place government-sponsored students competitively on UACE performance, and also admit private-sponsored students directly; private universities run their own admissions. Applicants apply online to the university, and choose programmes whose subject combinations match their A-Level subjects. Holders of recognised diplomas, mature-age candidates and international qualifications may also be considered under separate routes. The Uganda National Council for Higher Education (NCHE) accredits universities and programmes. Check the current prospectus for the exact subject and grade requirements.
admissions_overview.notes: Application dates, the programmes on offer, government sponsorship places and minimum requirements change every year. Check the admissions page of the university and the NCHE website for accredited institutions and programmes.
